newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal CPI shows need for wage restraint - BOP.
newsitem.headline: Portugal CPI shows need for wage restraint - BOP.

text.p: A quickening in non-tradeable price inflation in November, which lay behind the slightly higher than expected consumer price index (CPI), underlines the need for wage restraint, the Bank of Portugal said in its latest monthly report.

Non-tradeable prices, of which wages are a significant component, rose 4.9 percent year-on-year in November, up from 4.2 percent in October. The CPI rose 3.0 percent year-on-year, unchanged on the previous month.
The cost of eating out made a significant contribution to the increase in non-tradeable prices, the Bank said.
Nevertheless, it added that the quickening of non-tradeable prices "underlines the need for salary restraint."

The government and unions are still wide apart in 1997 public sector wage talks with labour leaders holding out for increases of at least 3.5 percent while the government says it cannot afford more than 2.8 percent.
